subject: Escalation: candidate feedback conflict & timing — Oliver Cho (SWE II)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: candidate feedback conflict & timing — Oliver Cho (SWE II)

Hi Laura / Vivek,

Quick escalation — the interview panel for Oliver Cho (SWE II) is split 3:2. Two strong technical endorsements; one interview flagged as "below bar" on system design and flagged for leveling concerns. Recruiter (Aisha) is pushing to move to offer because candidate has a counteroffer timeline (need yes/no within 72 hours). I read the feedback and there are contradictions: one engineer mentioned insufficient design depth, another called the implementation elegant and production-minded.

I'm concerned about two things:
- We risk offering at SWE II if panel concerns indicate SWE I expectations; that creates mis-leveling risk.
- Candidate timeline is tight — if we stall, we'll likely lose him.

Can HR advise: do we proceed with a conditional offer at the higher band with an explicit leveling/career-path clause, or do we run a quick calibration call with the interviewing committee? I need guidance on approval path for a discretionary comp override if we decide to boost the offer to secure him.

Attaching the interview feedback and the candidate portfolio.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Hiring Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: interview-feedback-oliver.pdf (3 pages), oliver-portfolio.zip (6 files)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: candidate feedback conflict & timing — Oliver Cho (SWE II)

Thanks for the context, Stephanie.

Quick read: I see the same divergence in feedback. Before we escalate to comp, two operational steps I recommend:
1) Pull the raw interview notes and ask the single dissenter for specific examples (line-by-line) of the level concerns — wording like "below bar" is too high level for a leveling decision.
2) If the dissenter confirms concrete examples we can't reconcile, run a 30-min calibration with the engineering interviewers (not the recruiter) to align on rubric interpretation.

If you need an exception to the band to move faster, I can provisionally approve a short-term sign-on buffer (one-time signing bonus or temporary uplift) but any base salary above band requires VP sign-off. Vivek — would you be available for a 30-min calibration or a quick verbal signoff if Stephanie proposes a one-time buffer to lock the candidate?

I can also draft a conditional offer template that states level will be confirmed after a 90-day performance checkpoint. That protects us against mis-leveling while giving the candidate certainty.

Laura Bennett
HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference

Attachment: comp-band-swe2.png (salary band reference)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: candidate feedback conflict & timing — Oliver Cho (SWE II)

Laura — thanks. I just pinged the dissenter (internal interviewer: Marcus Lin) and asked for the clarifying notes; Marcus replied with two concrete examples of architecture tradeoffs he felt were shallow (included below). That helps.

Given the 72-hr candidate timeline, I'm leaning toward:
- Offer at upper SWE I / lower SWE II base band + one-time sign-on (to match counteroffer).
- Clear 90-day performance review clause that pins final level to post-hire evaluation.

If we go this route, I'll need:
- Vivek: verbal approval for the sign-on buffer + agreement on the 90-day clause language, or a quick calibration call today to finalize.
- Laura: I can use your conditional template — please send draft ASAP so I can share with Aisha and Oliver.

Forwarding Marcus' comment below for visibility.

--Marcus' note (quoted):
"On the design question, Oliver provided a single-layer decomposition and did not discuss failure modes or scaling tradeoffs (cache invalidation, read-after-write). That is typically SWE II behavior. However, his coding and system ownership examples align with mid-SWE I to low-SWE II."

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Request: VP signoff for temporary comp uplift — Oliver Cho candidate

Vivek — Stephanie proposes offering candidate at a slightly elevated package to match his counteroffer and keep him in the funnel. HR can approve a one-time signing bonus up to $8k without exec signoff, but any base salary above the SWE II top band requires VP approval. Suggested path:
- Approve temporary offer: base at SWE I/II overlap band midpoint + $7k one-time sign-on.
- Conditional clause: level to be finalized at 90 days; if performance meets SWE II, adjust comp retroactively (if within budget).
- Require engineering calibration note and Marcus' written confirmation that the 90-day criteria are reasonable.

We need a quick verbal from you to proceed. If you approve, I will draft the conditional offer letter today and loop in Legal for final wording.

Laura Bennett
HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: VP signoff for temporary comp uplift — Oliver Cho candidate

Thanks for laying out the options. I'm okay proceeding with the proposed temporary package under these conditions:
- Base placed at the SWE I/II overlap midpoint (per comp-band-swe2.png).
- $7k one-time sign-on.
- 90-day performance checkpoint with explicit success criteria (Stephanie to propose 3 measurable outcomes).
- Marcus must provide a short calibration note confirming those outcomes map reasonably to SWE II expectations.

Laura — please prepare the conditional offer and tag Legal. Stephanie — draft the 3 outcomes today and I will review by EOD. I'll give verbal go-ahead to Aisha once offer language is reviewed.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Cho <oliver.cho@gmail.com>, Aisha Recruitment <aisha@novatolabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 17:20:00 -0800
Subject: Update and next steps — Oliver Cho (SWE II)

Hi Oliver / Aisha —

Apologies for the delay and for the back-and-forth — I wanted to be sure we were aligned internally before responding. We value the time you've invested in the process and appreciate your patience.

Proposed next steps (tentative):
- We can move to a conditional offer that would place you at the SWE I/II overlap base and include a $7,000 one-time sign-on to address timing.
- Final level will be confirmed after a 90-day performance checkpoint; the team will define three clear objectives for that period, and we will document outcomes in the offer. If objectives are met and the team agrees on SWE II performance, we'll adjust title/comp retroactively where appropriate.

Aisha — if Oliver is open to that approach, please let me know and I will ask HR to issue a conditional offer document today. If Oliver needs a hard yes/no or different timing because of the counteroffer, please surface that as well and we'll prioritize.

Thanks again — hope we can make this work.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Hiring Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: conditional-offer-draft (to be provided by HR)
